youtube.title: Stop Looking at the Pole #Shorts
youtube.description:
Mila has a whole empty square. She's about to hit the only pole.

Your steering tends to follow your eyes. In a driving simulator, drivers told to keep to the middle of the road while looking off to one side drifted toward where they looked (Readinger et al., 2002). On winding roads, drivers' eyes find each bend a second or two before they reach it (Land & Lee, 1994, Nature). Motorcycle trainers call staring at the thing you want to avoid 'target fixation' and teach riders to look where they want to go. So look at the gap, not the pole.

What's the pole you can't stop staring at?

Sources:
- Land & Lee (1994), Where we look when we steer, Nature 369: https://www.nature.com/articles/369742a0
- Readinger et al. (2002), Gaze-eccentricity effects on road position and steering, J. Exp. Psychol.: Applied: https://pure.mpg.de/pubman/item/item_1793077_3/component/file_3193624/pdf1012.pdf
- Wilkie & Wann (2003), Controlling steering and judging heading: https://centaur.reading.ac.uk/13818
- MSF, Looking where you want to go: https://magazine.americanmotorcyclist.com/?p=9661

Mila, Grandpa and the square are fictional.
